payload.summary: Evaluated three budget-tracking amendments against the codebase. The oxygen guard omission (fr-10-12259602) is a genuine gap worth addressing given the acceptance criteria explicitly mention oxygen tracking. The compile-time gating concern (fr-10-70478168) is largely a non-issue since the implementation satisfies the spirit of zero-cost-when-disabled. The per-pool test granularity concern (fr-10-75c62b7a) is valid but already mitigated by the structural coverage test.

votes.rationale: The acceptance criteria (tanksim-6e5.1.2.1) explicitly state 'Track oxygen demand in the same framework where feasible.' The BudgetDelta already carries an oxygen ElementBudget, and oxygen_mg is computed in BudgetSnapshot::from_state. The dissolved_oxygen system has reaeration (an open-system atmospheric exchange) which makes oxygen inherently non-conserving — but that's exactly the situation carbon faces with DIC atmospheric shortcuts, which the carbon guard handles via chemistry_external_carbon_flux_mg(). The infrastructure to subtract known open-system oxygen fluxes (reaeration) already exists in the budget entry labels. Silently ignoring oxygen residuals means bugs in oxygen accounting (e.g., a system consuming DO without recording it) go undetected. At minimum, the intentional omission should be documented with a comment in enforce_tracked_tick_budget_guard explaining why oxygen is excluded. Better yet, add an oxygen guard with a wider tolerance that accounts for reaeration flux, mirroring the carbon guard pattern.

The acceptance criteria say 'the instrumentation compiles out or is zero-cost when not in use' — the implementation satisfies the 'zero-cost when not in use' alternative. When budget_ledger is None: no BudgetSnapshot::from_state calls occur (gated by if tick.is_some()), no allocations happen, and no budget deltas are computed. The unconditionally compiled types (BudgetLedger, BudgetSnapshot, ElementBudget, helper functions) are dead code that the linker can strip in release builds and represent negligible binary size regardless. The test test_budget_ledger_zero_cost_when_disabled correctly verifies the meaningful claim: no runtime overhead when disabled. Adding a cargo feature flag would increase build matrix complexity for no practical benefit. The amendment itself acknowledges this is 'a defensible design choice' and the concern is speculative ('if the acceptance criteria strictly require compile-time gating'). They don't — the disjunctive criterion is met.

The amendment identifies a real but already-mitigated concern. The structural coverage test (test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields) is the authoritative safety net: it serializes TankState to JSON, discovers all element-bearing fields by naming convention, and asserts exact set equality with budget component labels. If any microbe pool were omitted from nitrogen_budget_components(), this test would fail because the field path would appear in the discovered set but not in the component labels. The aggregate-sum test (test_total_n_helper_sums_all_pools) serves a different purpose — verifying that conversion math is correct for the total — and the linearity of conversions means aggregation doesn't mask errors. Adding per-pool assertions would make the test more brittle without adding meaningful safety beyond what the structural test already provides. The defense-in-depth argument is reasonable in principle but the existing structural test already delivers that depth.
